title: Rescue Operation
dateline: A rooftop over the Academy district.
mood: A small gold star beeps for the first time in weeks, and Guinevere flies off alone to follow it.

hero.alt: Seen from high above, a column of dark violet smoke rises over a city of lit towers beside the water, past a tall tower crowned with a ring.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 43

segs.t: Vexana stood on the roof of a lecture block, staff in hand. Inside her right sleeve, pinned against her wrist, the small gold star was warm.
Before first light the door had taken her back into the dark, as it always did. At the alarm the Will sent her out again, with the first wave, along the rim of the gateway.
The order had come as a voice inside her. “The Academy. Now.” A place and a time. Never a why.
She had brought the wave down on the waterfront warehouses. The alarm had emptied them already.
Only roofs,
she had told herself.
Now the Enders crouched around her on the tiles. When she moved, they moved. That was the Will’s mark on her: its Enders ran with her as if she led them.

Her own machines had come through with her. She called them her Eternal Guards. The lead one stood folded behind a chimney at her back, purple plate edged in gold, a magenta heart crest on its chest. Its eyes were dark. She was saving her power.

Her three giants waited folded and dark on the high ledges over the platforms, the broad stone tiers that joined the city’s wards above the bay. Their swords lay across their knees. They would drop at her hand.
Over the bay the storm had put out the morning. She knew whose storm it was. Yesterday, in the void, she had watched the Storm Citadel leave the Mother Matrix and settle behind the gateway’s mouth.

Her plan had not changed. When the Mother Matrix came through whole and close, and opened its chest to fire, she would go into it with everything she had. She would not come out of it. Until then she stayed near it, and obeyed.
And before then, Guinevere had to be out of the fight. In the vision she had lain broken among the others.
“The Academy,” the order had said. For Vexana, the Academy was one girl. For once the order and her own wish pointed at the same place. She did not ask why.
She could have watched from the ruined tower beyond the dome, well past the beep’s reach, as she had for weeks. Today she had taken the nearest roof.
One look,
she had told herself. She had known what the star would do this close.
At her wrist, inside the sleeve, the Emblem beeped.
It was small and bright, and it carried over the sirens. Across the courtyard, a second beep answered.
She pressed her arm tight against her side. Around her, no Ender turned its head.
Down there Guinevere stood with the frontline, one hand at her collar. She was crying. She was smiling too.
Vexana’s fingers closed on the staff until the grip creaked.
“Betray her...” she said, very low.
“But to protect her...”
She said the rest to the star in her sleeve. “Even hidden in the dark of night, I will remain an unwavering guardian.”

media.alt: Vexana, her hair pale lavender and her violet eyes wet, looks down from the roof; a caption reads: Betray her...
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 44

media.alt: Vexana stands with her staff, its orb dark as a hole; a tall purple and gold machine with a magenta heart crest looms behind her; a caption reads: But to protect her...
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 44

segs.t: Wherever Vexana went, that beep would bring Guinevere. And Vexana had to be under the gateway when the Matrix came. If Guinevere came with the whole frontline, they would all be standing there together when it did. That was the vision.
If she came alone, and early, she could be put down first. Hurt, out of the fight. Alive.
Vexana stepped to the roof’s edge, so the gateway’s glow lit her from behind. A shape and a staff, nothing more. Let her be seen. Let her be followed.
She jumped for the platforms. The Enders poured after her.
The courtyard.
Fanny stood under a sky the color of slate. Shield soldiers and students in suits held their ranks around her. Layla stood at her left, the cannon on her shoulder.
Over the ranks hung the courtyard billboard: Guinevere and Vexana back to back, Vexana’s hair long and black.
Something beeped beside Fanny, high and thin, under the sirens.
It came from Guinevere’s collar. She pressed her hand over the gold star there, and her face crumpled.

media.alt: Guinevere, tears in her eyes, presses her gloved hand to the gold star at her collar.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 45

segs.t: “Guinevere?” said Fanny.

Guinevere was staring at a roof across the courtyard. A figure stepped to its edge, against the glow over the bay. A staff in its hand. Too dark to read. Enders crouched all around it. Nobody had seen them come.
“That’s her,” whispered Guinevere. “That’s her.”
Her.
Fanny had not heard that beep in weeks. It was the pair’s sound.
She looked from the billboard to the roof. Enders, and a dark shape standing easy among them.
Up there, with them?
She shut the thought before it finished.
Under Guinevere’s hand the star was flashing. Her mouth shook, and it was a smile.
She turned to Fanny and Layla. She opened her mouth.
Fanny’s hand had already gone to her blade. Down the ranks, the Shield soldiers swung their rifles up at the roof.
Guinevere looked at the rifles. She closed her mouth, and her fingers tightened over the star.
On the roof the figure jumped, toward the bay. Guinevere’s wings of light opened, and she shot after it.
“Guinevere!” Fanny shouted.
Her voice came back over the open channel as she climbed. “Ruby said it’s a lure. If it is, it’s mine.”
“Guinevere,” said Lesley on the channel. “Knowing when to retreat is an important skill, too.”
No answer came. The light of her wings shrank over the roofs and was gone.
She had left her post without an order. Fanny had never once done that, and had never once wanted to.

Fanny looked up for anyone who could see farther than she could. On the bell tower a girl sat with her heels against the stone, a lollipop stick at her lips. Selena. Her dragon-shaped machine crouched beside her. Neither moved.
Mobile support,
thought Fanny.
A spotter takes the best seat in the city and sits still until she sees something. Good. The deck should know.
She reached for the channel.
“Fanny!” Layla had her by the sleeve. “The hall! The big display’s tracking her. Now!”
In the hall, students packed the dark under the big display. It showed the Singularity, a four-pointed rift in a swirl of pink and violet. A small figure flew straight at it.
Then Guinevere’s face filled the screen, wet and set.
“I’m prepared to enter the Singularity.”
The display switched to a map of the city. A red zone spread over the waterfront and the platforms.

media.alt: In a dark hall, students watch a big display: a four-pointed rift in a swirl of pink and violet, a small figure flying at it; then a map of the city washed in red, with a warning sign.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: Angela stood at the panel, Tetra at her shoulder. “According to the readings, the Singularity’s energy signature is spiking rapidly. The Enders are mobilizing. What is our course of action?”
“So many hostiles! She must be in danger!” Fanny’s voice was already the command voice. “Shield squad holds the courtyard. Angela, with me. Layla, take the...”
“I’ve already identified several weak points in their defenses.” Layla held up her tablet. The red map on it was marked with green. “This rescue operation is ready to go!”
Fanny looked at the marks.
Hold the line and send a squad. That’s the Shield’s way.
It was slower than Layla’s, by a lot. Layla had built that map in the time it took Fanny to give one order.
Layla flicked the map to the deck.
Lesley’s voice came back at once. “Frontline goes on Layla’s plan. Rear support, stay on their heels. The deck holds. If this is a lure, the second front comes here.”
Ruby came through the hall at a run, the scythe on her shoulder. “Your sector, Commander,” she said on the channel, dry.
Lesley’s rifle had been on Ruby since the day she landed. Fanny had heard why. Ruby took the order without a word against it.
They ran for the main gate. Beside it the gate portal stood, a tall frame already filling with light. Step in, and it put you out where the fight was.
Layla stepped up to go first. She had gone first on every raid since the Enders came only in handfuls, so that Fanny would be covered.
Fanny felt the frown come, the same one as every raid.
Somebody out in front, covering me.
She had never liked it. Out in front was her place.
Layla glanced back at the frown. She was going to let her have it, the way she always did.
Her map,
thought Fanny.
I dropped my own order for it.
She let her brow go smooth.
Her front.
She spoke before Layla reached the light.
“Lead,” she said.
